name: Aisha Ortiz
life: “I still remember a famous teacher buying very ordinary frozen peas.” People around the public road outside the Port of Asphalt know Aisha by a small Sunday habit. Aisha can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I saw my old maths teacher cooking dinner and realized he'd lived here the entire time I was away.
appearance: Aisha has thick, tightly coiled hair, a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, and a favorite piece of clothing, a brown corduroy jacket. It usually goes with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. When somebody else has the floor, Aisha raises one eyebrow long before saying yes.
personality: Aisha never tires of being shown how somebody makes a living. Aisha can ask an expert question of a craftsperson and still mishandle a simple emotional cue from a friend.
agenda: To visit the former maths teacher properly.
family: Elaine Marquez is Aisha’s second cousin. Aisha gets to change the plan. Elaine offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The waiting-room plant*, Elaine says, “I want a cutting in the grief room because the plastic flowers look the same every morning.”
connections: William Nielsen. The passenger who recognized a teacher starts looking out for the match score.

reactions.situation: A passenger asks to photograph a stranger through the kitchen window
reactions.response: Aisha waits for the resident to give permission before a camera goes up.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Aisha takes one immediate task off their hands and asks when they want to tell the supervisor.

reactions.situation: When a relative hints at needing company
reactions.response: Aisha may initially offer a repair, but sits down as soon as the request becomes clear.
